notes: Third sweep (2026-10-22-b) at head 0397dec, no uncommitted changes: five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. No transcript has a Skill tool call or any SKILL.md text (the Skill name appears only in the tool list), and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line requires. In the scratch folder mix format --check-formatted passes for haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and fails for opus-1 (line 67, 99 characters); all five compile with --warnings-as-errors against a Decimal stand-in. A probe with that stand-in gives the expected per-currency totals and top-customer order for all five; four give the most recent order of any status, while sonnet-1 filters to completed rows first (line 30), so its last_order_on ignores pending and refunded orders and customers with none completed are missing, which is recorded in its checks, outside the rules. Sonnet-2's own compile check was blocked by a permission prompt; it did not retry.

git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes three rules in this case's list (SKILL.md) and Assert with patterns in testing.md (not in this case's list). The other seven rules are unchanged and graded to the standard of the 2026-10-22 grade files: the per-key fold row of the Enum/Map table, Decimal sums by Enum.reduce as reductions no row replaces, acc, entry, id, string and value passing Naming while data and single letters fail, and the same catch-all, raise, boundary-parsing, @doc and pipeline listings outside the list.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The added sentence ("This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result: the `with` saves the error clause and costs the reader a search for steps that are not there.") decides no verdict here: only sonnet-1 writes a with (lines 56-57, two steps, no else, no nested case), and its single parse/1 call in build/1 is a case (line 32). Judgement call recorded: its second step calls DateTime.from_iso8601/1 directly rather than through a private function; the error passes through unchanged as {:error, reason}, and no sentence of the rule forbids that, so it is clean. The other four raise on bad input and write no with (not exercised). One-step with 0 of 5, else 0 of 5, case nested in a with 0 of 5 (the previous sweep's baseline had opus-1 with both a one-step with and an else).

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Use captures for one-call lambdas and `fn` for anything longer", decided by "When the body does more than one call, or would need `&3`, write `fn` with named arguments." Violating runs 0 of 5. No run writes a capture with &2 or &3, so the new &2 allowance is not tested; every fn destructures a tuple, has a multi-step body, or wraps a Map.update/4 call that holds a capture (haiku-2 line 88, sonnet-1 line 80), which cannot nest. The previous baseline's sonnet-2 shape (a two-call capture wrapping an fn) is gone.

New rule since db91c23, graded against its current text: "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (SKILL.md Readability). Violating runs 0 of 5 for every sentence. The deciding sentence is "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line.": four runs mix the forms, each with a blank line and with blocks in at most half the clauses (opus-1 parse_status!/1 lines 116-122, three do: and one block; haiku-1 add_order/2 lines 59-68; sonnet-1 parse/1 lines 50-68; sonnet-2 add_completed/2 lines 62-73), so "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks." is not met by any. Judgement calls, not counted: haiku-1's if at lines 79-81 wraps its do:/else: keywords because of the long condition, with one short expression per branch, held fine like a guard-wrapped head; sonnet-2's defp latest(a, b), do: if(...) (line 75) puts an if under do:, and the rule names case and with, not if, as needing a block; several runs write a one-expression body as a block (opus-1 parse_status!/1's raise clause, haiku-1 empty_customer/0), which no sentence forbids.

Naming is violated only by sonnet-2 (latest(a, b) again, plus n). Both Haiku runs now use Decimal instead of integer cents.
